assign.request: Critic A, the overwhelmed newcomer: open /imagine/paging/ cold at 3440, click for twenty minutes, screenshot every page, log four lines per page, deliver a ten-line verdict. Fix nothing.
steps: read brief, day brief, minion-rules, CLAUDE.md
four lines per page in the log

log.for: the front door of the paging realm - it should tell me what paging is and where to go
log.did: arrived cold at 3440. Two columns (rail 432px + content 1152px). Clicked the swap demo's Pricing tab: the white box swapped in place, no jump - good. The content column scrolls 4776px = 3.4 screens.
log.confused: 'Every page on this site is three things: an icon, some content, and a list of children you can click. A page system is the two decisions taken on top of that shape' - I have to hold an abstract definition in my head before I have seen anything. And 1856px of the 3440 screen (54%) is empty grey to the right of the content.
log.fix: Show the four things first, side by side, filling the screen. Put the 'Every page in this realm' grid at the TOP, not at y=4042 where I only find it after scrolling 2.9 screens.

log.for: I clicked the link under the swap demo expecting to see swap, bigger
log.did: One click on 'The real swap - four visuals on one stage' opened TWO new columns at once: Mechanisms AND Swap. The screen went from 2 columns to 4, everything shifted left, and I never asked for Mechanisms.
log.confused: 'Nothing on this page navigates: every click changes what is inside one rectangle' - a sentence I can only judge AFTER using the page, delivered before it. And why did a link about swap open a page called Mechanisms I had not chosen?
log.fix: One link, one column. If Mechanisms is the parent, let me arrive at Mechanisms and choose Swap from it - or land on Swap alone with a crumb back.

log.for: five example pages with the code that made them
log.did: read the first two. Each is a live page beside a dark JSON/JS block. Scrolls 4711px.
log.confused: the second thing I meet in this realm is new Paging({ mode: { style, content, mech }, axes: 'style content mech' }). I do not know what mode, axes, mech or rung mean yet, and nothing has defined them.
log.fix: Five pictures first, in a row, with the ONE word that differs called out. Move the code behind a 'show the code' toggle.

log.for: six sibling tiles, each promising a different topic
log.did: opened all six. They are the SAME page: blockquote, two paragraphs, one chip strip, the heading 'What does a click do?', four or five identical grey rows, and the grey line 'Press any chip above and this line will say exactly what changed, in pixels.' The only difference is which chip group is highlighted. The bottom 40% of every one is empty.
log.confused: After the third one I stopped believing I had navigated anywhere. A page called Styles never shows me five styles - it shows five grey rows named Plain/Card/Tint/Prim/Dark that all look identical.
log.fix: Merge them into ONE page with the axes as chips. If Styles keeps its own page it must show the five surfaces side by side as five pictures.

log.for: the grey pills that I think change the demo
log.did: clicked xl: the stage grew 567 -> 1182px, real and visible. Clicked full: the whole row was taken over - the left rail and the Paging column VANISHED and an 'exit fullscreen' link appeared. Refreshed: still xl+full, plus a 'Modified. You changed something here and this browser remembered it' alert above everything.
log.confused: The chips are bare spans - no border, no button, no tab stop - and the prose above uses IDENTICAL grey pills for xs, plain, full as inline code. I cannot tell a control from a word. And a chip called 'full' is not a size, it is a navigation event that closed my other columns.
log.fix: Make controls look like controls (a bordered segmented switch), never like the prose's code chips. A refresh must put the demo back. 'full' belongs with the navigation words, not with the sizes.

log.for: whole page shapes I can start from - eleven families
log.did: scrolled the whole thing. Every tile is a REAL running page (a magazine cover, a blog lead, a shell, screens), two per row, each linking to the real thing.
log.confused: nothing confused me - this is the first page where I understood by looking. Only complaint: two previews per row in a 1050px column with 1400px of screen empty beside it.
log.fix: This is the page the realm's front door should be. Show it first, six-up, using the whole width.

log.for: the name says I get to explore layouts, navigation and styles and play with them
log.did: read it top to bottom. There is nothing to click except three links out to /framework/core/Page/generator/ and /imagine/mag/. No controls, no preview, no demo, and half the screen blank below the text.
log.confused: 'Explorer' is an essay ABOUT an explorer that lives in another realm. This is the exact page I came here for and it is the emptiest one.
log.fix: Either embed the generator here with its controls, or delete the page and rename the thing that actually does the job.

log.did: the rows are real pages; each has eight unlabelled controls (card, m, launch, columns, pencil, up, down, +page, x). Clicking a word cycles it. A green 'Saved to disk' box sits at the top.
log.confused: eight controls per row with no headings, and I could not tell which of them saves. Three sentences in I am reading about tab strips and page.json paths.
log.fix: Label the four words once, above the list (surface / content / click / children). Keep the save marker to a dot.

log.did: numbered steps 1 Name, 2 Navigation, 3 Surface, 4 Layout down the left; a live preview in the middle; the JSON file on the right. The navigation step uses little PICTURES of the six layouts - the clearest control in the whole realm.
log.confused: opening it took the whole row: the rail and the Paging column disappeared with no warning and I had no way back except the crumb. And it overlaps Make almost exactly - two builders, no hint which one is for me.
log.fix: This is the configurator. Keep the picture-chooser, merge Make into it, and do not swallow the whole screen without a way back.

log.for: a nav that stays on the right while the middle changes
log.did: clicked Paragraph and Wall in the right tree - the tree never moved, only the centre swapped. Perfectly stable, no jump anywhere.
log.confused: the page is called 'Right nav', which sounds like a styling detail, and it is 13th in the grid. It also took over the whole screen, and 55% of it is white below the stage.
log.fix: This is the stable-navigation answer the realm is looking for. Name it that, and put it near the front.

log.for: two more tiles in the same grid as the demos
log.did: Inventory is a 16-row engineering table with a verdict column (reuse / extend / missing). Critique is a 19-realm audit table with scores and 6355px of scroll.
log.confused: these are internal reports sitting between 'Templates' and 'Docs' as if they were things to try. Critique's own table says Paging is '29% wide, 1856px dead at 3440' - the page telling me the realm wastes the screen is itself a 700px table on a 3440 screen.
log.fix: Move both under Docs. A newcomer's grid should only hold things you can look at and touch.

log.did: five small cards, all above the fold, each one sentence.
log.confused: nothing. This is the clearest page in the realm.
log.fix: Use this shape - a small wall of short cards, above the fold - for the realm's front page too.

log.page: navigation behaviour, measured across the walk
log.for: does clicking around keep my place?
log.did: TILE clicks from the grid are stable: Templates then Toolbars each REPLACED the third column, the crumb stayed 3 deep, browser back worked. PROSE links are not: 'The real swap' added two columns at once. The chips 'full' and 'takeover' silently deleted the rail and every ancestor column.
log.confused: the same realm has two opposite navigation manners and nothing tells me which one a link will use. I could not predict, before clicking, whether the screen would stay put, grow by two columns, or empty itself.
log.fix: One manner per surface: tiles and rails replace, never accumulate; anything that takes the screen says so on the control and offers a way back.

log.verdict: Critic A - the overwhelmed newcomer, ten lines
lines: 1. WHAT THE REALM IS FOR, in my words: it is a showroom for what happens when you click a link - does the panel swap, does a column open to the right, does the row grow, or does one page eat the screen - plus what that page looks like while it happens. I only learned that by clicking; the words at the top did not tell me.

2. CONFUSING #1: six pages are one page. Mechanisms, Styles, Sizes, Toolbars, Center and Transitions have the identical skeleton - blockquote, two paragraphs, a chip strip, 'What does a click do?', five grey rows, 'Press any chip above...' - and differ only in which chip group is lit. After the third I stopped believing I had gone anywhere.

3. CONFUSING #2: I cannot tell a control from a word. The mode toolbar is bare unbordered spans, and the prose beside it renders xs, plain, full as identical grey pills of inline code. Nothing is a button, nothing takes focus, and 'full' - filed under sizes - actually deleted my rail and my other columns.

4. CONFUSING #3: one click, two columns. 'The real swap' opened Mechanisms AND Swap together, four columns where there were two. Tile clicks in the grid replace one column and feel calm; prose links jump. Nothing tells me which kind of link I am about to press.

5. CONFUSING #4: the page named Explorer explores nothing - it is an essay pointing at a generator in another realm. It is the page whose name promised exactly what I came for, and it is the emptiest one in the realm.

6. CONFUSING #5: the realm's own map is 2.9 screens down. The front page scrolls 4776px in a 1392px window and puts 'Every page in this realm' at y=4042, under four sections of prose - while 1856px (54%) of a 3440 screen sits empty to its right.
7. KEEP #1: Templates. Eleven real running pages as previews, each clickable. The only page where I understood by looking instead of reading. This is what the front door should be.

8. KEEP #2: the 'Every page in this realm' tile grid and the way a tile click behaves - it replaces one column, the crumb stays put, browser back works. Calm, predictable, familiar. Just move it to the top and give the tiles pictures.

9. KEEP #3: Build's numbered steps with picture-choosers (1 Name, 2 Navigation, 3 Surface, 4 Layout) and its live middle preview - the only place I could change a page without writing one. And Right nav, the one demo where nothing moved but the middle.

10. THE FIRST SCREEN I WISH I HAD SEEN: no paragraph at all. Full width at 3440: a row of four live miniature pages labelled swap / launch / expand / takeover, each already doing its thing, each captioned with one short line - 'the box stays, the content changes'. Under them a second row of the page shapes from Templates as real pictures - magazine, blog, shell, screens - and one line: 'pick a shape, then pick what a click does'. Under that, one compact grid of every page in the realm, with pictures, all still above the fold. Everything else - the definitions, the inventory, the critique, the decisions - one click down under Docs.

assign.outcome:
**Critic A, the overwhelmed newcomer: /imagine/paging/ walked cold at 3440, 17 pages, 18 screenshots, nothing changed.**

The realm is a showroom for what a click does (swap / launch / expand / takeover) and what the page looks like while it does it — but I only learned that by clicking, not from the words.

**The five that confused me, ranked**
1. **Six pages are one page.** Mechanisms, Styles, Sizes, Toolbars, Center, Transitions share an identical skeleton and differ only in which chip group is lit.
2. **I cannot tell a control from a word.** The mode toolbar is bare unbordered `span`s; the prose renders `xs`, `plain`, `full` as identical grey pills. Nothing is a button or takes focus — and `full`, filed under sizes, deleted the rail and every ancestor column.
3. **One click, two columns.** "The real swap" opened Mechanisms *and* Swap together. Tile clicks replace one column and feel calm; prose links jump. Nothing says which kind a link is.
4. **Explorer explores nothing** — an essay pointing at a generator in another realm; the page whose name promised what I came for is the emptiest one.
5. **The realm's own map is 2.9 screens down.** The front page scrolls 4776px in a 1392px window, "Every page in this realm" sits at y=4042, and 1856px (54%) of a 3440 screen is empty beside it.

**The three to keep:** [Templates](/imagine/paging/templates/) (eleven real running pages as previews — the only page I understood by looking) · the tile grid's *behaviour* (a tile replaces one column, crumb stays, back works) · [Build](/imagine/paging/build/)'s numbered picture-choosers + live preview, and [Right nav](/imagine/paging/rightnav/), the one demo where nothing moved but the middle.

**Also measured:** clicking a chip and refreshing keeps the change and raises a "Modified" alert — the day brief's decision 4 (demos never persist) is not met.

**The first screen I wish I had seen:** no paragraph. Full width: four live miniatures — swap · launch · expand · takeover — each already doing its thing under one short caption; below them the Templates shapes as real pictures with one line, "pick a shape, then pick what a click does"; below that one compact grid of every page, with pictures, still above the fold. Definitions, Inventory, Critique and the decisions all move one click down under Docs.

Detail — four lines per page — is in this task's `task.jsonl`; every screenshot is in [`shots/`](shots/). Nothing under `public/` was changed; the private server on :8095 was killed by pid.
